title: Rainbow Children's Medicare Ltd - 543524 - Announcement under Regulation 30 (LODR)-Earnings Call Transcript

summary.headline: Rainbow Q1 FY27 revenue rose 33% YoY to INR 470 crore and EBITDA 30% to INR 134.6 crore at a 28.6% margin; like-for-like growth was 24%.
summary.overview: Operating revenue grew 33% YoY to INR 470 crore, with acquisitions (Guwahati, Warangal) contributing about INR 38 crore. EBITDA rose 30% to INR 134.6 crore at a 28.6% margin, despite losses at newly commissioned hospitals, and PAT rose 16% to INR 62.5 crore. Operating metrics grew: inpatient discharges 28%, outpatient consultations 25%, deliveries 23%, with ARPOB up 6%. Management guided to above 20% revenue growth in Q2 and a return to 24-25% EBITDA margin (pre-Ind AS) by year-end, and set out a plan to add 2,500 beds over five years.

financial_highlights.value: 6% improvement cited; mature hospitals approx. INR 70,000 vs under-5-year hospitals approx. INR 59,000

segments.name: Mature hospitals
segments.commentary: ARPOB approx. INR 70,000 in Q1, about 18% above hospitals less than five years old; management attributed the roughly 10% mature-cluster ARPOB rise to a mix of pricing and case mix.

segments.name: Newer / greenfield hospitals
segments.commentary: Rajahmundry is at roughly breakeven; Electronic City (Bengaluru) expected to break even in 2-3 months. Management guides new Bengaluru hospitals to break even within 12-15 months, all within about 18 months.

segments.name: Acquisitions (Guwahati, Warangal)
segments.commentary: Both are EBITDA-positive. Guwahati is at near company-average margins and grew about 20%; Warangal is ramping toward company-level margins over the next year.

guidance_outlook: Revenue growth expected above 20% in Q2 FY27; management expects 20%-plus growth to be sustained, and about 20% annually would double revenue in roughly four years.
Expects to cross INR 2,000 crore revenue by end of FY27.
EBITDA margin expected to return to 24%-25% on a pre-Ind AS basis by year-end.
Plans to add 2,500 beds over five years to reach 5,000 beds, with capex of about INR 2,200 crore; 1,200 beds already in various stages of development.
Mumbai (Malad, 100-bed brownfield) expected to start in Q1 FY28; Management said Mumbai EBITDA margins should eventually exceed 20%, with no precise near-term figure.
Indore to commence Q3 FY27; Coimbatore hub and Gurgaon Sector 56 spoke in Q3 FY28; Gurgaon Sector 44 hub in Q1 FY29; Pune (150 beds) and Bengaluru Seegehalli spoke in FY29.
Nellore (70-bed acquisition, expanding to 100+ beds) and 30-bed maternal block expected in about six months; Guntur 50-bed leased hospital to start in a couple of months.
capex_capacity: Total bed capacity grew 26% YoY to 2,435 beds; operational beds up 22% to 1,862 beds; management said bed capacity reached 500 with recent additions (as stated).

Over next five years: add 2,500 beds to reach 5,000 beds, capex about INR 2,200 crore; approximately 30% of future additions in existing southern markets and 70% in new markets (Delhi NCR, North, Central India, Mumbai).
Capex in Q1 was about INR 56 crore, mainly on existing hospitals and upcoming projects; funded through internal accruals.
Mumbai Malad 100-bed brownfield hospital (definitive agreement signed); Nellore 70-bed Prime Children's Hospital acquired; Guntur 50-bed leased hospital.
Management said it is 'not far' from breakeven at Rajahmundry and Electronic City; Hennur and HRBR are still in investment phase.

qa_highlights.question: Will Q2 revenue growth remain in the mid-20s after the higher base?
qa_highlights.answer: Management expects Q2 revenue growth in the 20% range and above 20%, citing digital initiatives and lead conversion.

qa_highlights.question: Organic growth ex-acquisitions?
qa_highlights.answer: Acquisitions contributed about INR 38 crore; like-for-like revenue growth was 24%.

qa_highlights.question: Mature-cluster ARPOB up about 10%: why?
qa_highlights.answer: Management attributed it to a combination of pricing and case mix.

qa_highlights.question: Mumbai margin expectations and doctor model?
qa_highlights.answer: Management declined to give a precise margin, but said EBITDA margins should eventually exceed 20%. Core doctors will stay full-time, with some hybrid models for certain specialists.

qa_highlights.question: Bengaluru hospital breakeven timing and losses?
qa_highlights.answer: New Bengaluru hospitals still incur losses; guidance unchanged at 12-15 months to breakeven, with all within about 18 months.

qa_highlights.question: Is 20% growth the medium-term revenue target?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said sustaining about 20% annual growth would double revenue in about four years; that is the directional view, not a formal target.

risks_watch: Margin pressure from ramp-up of new hospitals (Rajahmundry, Electronic City, Hennur, HRBR); margin recovery to 24%-25% by year-end depends on operating leverage.
Monsoon delay could weaken Q2/Q3 seasonal demand; management has not yet quantified July trends.
Entry into high-cost markets (Mumbai, NCR) with higher employee and doctor costs; Mumbai margins are not yet defined.
Integration of acquired hospitals (Nellore, Guntur, Malad) and the Malad JV structure with three doctor-promoters; ownership and lock-in terms were not disclosed.
Execution across multiple new geographies with management bandwidth and doctor-recruitment constraints, particularly in the Northeast.
demand_pricing: Revenue INR 470 crore, up 33% YoY; acquisitions (Guwahati, Warangal) contributed about INR 38 crore, so like-for-like growth was 24%.
Inpatient discharges up 28%, outpatient consultations up 25%, deliveries up 23%; occupancy over 41%; ARPOB up 6%.
Mature-cluster ARPOB about INR 70,000 vs about INR 59,000 for hospitals under five years old (about 18% gap); mature-cluster ARPOB rise of about 10% attributed to pricing and case mix.
Payer mix: cash about 48%, insurance about 42%; government-scheme patients being evaluated only for excess capacity, subject to reimbursement rates.

Q2 FY27 revenue growth guided to the 20% range and above 20%; management said about 20% annual growth would double revenue in roughly four years, described as directional, not a formal target. Expects to cross INR 2,000 crore revenue by FY27 end.
Seasonality: monsoon delayed; management said July too early to draw conclusions and business plans are not built on stronger seasonality.

Newer hospitals: Rajahmundry at about breakeven; Electronic City expected to break even in 2-3 months; new Bengaluru hospitals (HRBR, Electronic City) break even within 12-15 months, all within about 18 months.

Acquisitions (Guwahati, Warangal) are EBITDA-positive; Guwahati near company-average margins; Warangal to reach company-level margins within a year. Management does not expect acquisitions to dilute EBITDA.
Mumbai (Malad): no precise margin given; EBITDA margins should eventually exceed 20%. Core doctors to stay full-time, with hybrid model possible for some specialty doctors.
key_quotes: we remain confident of delivering revenue growth in the 20% range during the second quarter as well. We expect growth to remain above 20%.

I am not in a position to provide a precise margin expectation today. However, I am confident that EBITDA margins should eventually be above 20%, although it is too early to estimate where they will ultimately stabilize.
We continue to expect EBITDA margins to return to the 24% –25% range on a pre -Ind AS basis by the end of the year.
It is still too early to comment. The monsoon has been delayed, which everyone is aware of, so we will need to wait and see how the season evolves.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand, ARPOB and the 20%-plus growth outlook, and reiterated the 24%-25% pre-Ind AS margin target for year-end. Cautious and non-committal on Mumbai margins, July/seasonality trends, and the Bengaluru breakeven timing, where management declined to give precise figures.

Nellore 70-bed acquisition expanding to 100+ beds plus 30-bed maternal block

growth.why: Q1 revenue grew 33% reported (24% like-for-like) with management guiding above 20% growth in Q2 and sustained, plus a 2,500-bed, ~INR 2,200 crore expansion over five years and a cross-INR 2,000 crore revenue target by FY27 end.
